title: Multiclass & progression
summary: Three classes, one character. Learn spells, earn skills and develop abilities.
body:
Search gear for your held classes

The loot finder defaults to Any held class, matching Nightcap equipment access. Select up to three classes; use All selected classes when every selected class must appear on the item. Slot, required level, deity and special item rules still apply.

Robe appearance — live testing: Game update 2026102204 repairs the native robe waist binding for seven Classic races. Close the game and update through the normal launcher. Held-class equipment eligibility stays the same. Affected races and testing status.

AA pacing and XP blessings updated: Each point requires 1,000,000 AA experience. Passive earning remains 10%; earned points, purchases and raw partial experience are retained. Goldwind’s paid XP package is retired; Matron Restora still offers free ordinary buffs. AA progression · Tunnel buffs.

THJ behavior and stock gear — live testing

The custom AA, spell focus and stock-derived gear update is installed for live testing. Scaling uses 131 researched Legendary items and matching standard EverQuest baselines. Classic level 50 and starter progression are preserved. Reopen the normal launcher for game 2026101902 before testing. See behavior details and open testing limits.

The AA changes include group Act of Valor, activated 40% Harvest, four percentage-based Mana Burns, universal caster Silent Casting, Warrior attack debuffs, Wizard Pyromancy/Cryomancy and a separate Wizard Dimensional Shielding. Spell Casting Subtlety and obsolete Silent Casting modifiers are retired; recorded purchase costs are refunded once on login. Class ownership, other purchases and starter grants remain intact. Exact uncertain costs and coefficients are listed in the candidate guide.

Live AA testing: All 16 classes have more earned AA options: 75 newly available lines, 111 expanded lines and Druid access to Healing Boon. The latest custom behavior update retires Spell Casting Subtlety and obsolete Silent Casting modifiers, with recorded-cost refunds. Classic remains level 50. Reconnect and turn Recommended AA off to browse your held classes. Read the AA update.

Live testing: Reviewed earned pet and melee AA ranks and held-class combat benefits are available for live testing. Normal ownership, costs, prerequisites and skill requirements remain. The active level cap is still 50; the separate Planes of Power profile is not activated.

Three classes from level 1

Keep your starting class and choose two different extra classes with the Ancient Chronicler in the tunnel.

Your whole build in view

See Primary, Second, and Third in Inventory and with #classes. Class information refreshes when you make a choice.

Best base health and mana from your classes

Your character uses the strongest base-health and base-mana calculations among the classes you hold. A melee starting class can gain a mana pool through a caster class.

Scribe early; cast at the required level

Buy and learn spells, songs and tomes for your held classes. Eligible scrolls can enter your spellbook before their required level. Memorizing into a spell gem and casting still require the spell’s normal level for a class you hold. An early-scribed spell is not an early unlock.

Equipment access across your classes

Wear equipment allowed by any of your held classes. Ordinary wearable items and augments allow every playable race when their class requirement matches. Slot, deity, required level, weapon conflicts and augment compatibility still apply. Update through the launcher for the matching equipment and inspection behavior.

Clearer spell levels

Scroll inspection removes unusable classes and shows the correct levels. The spell-selection menu also refreshes after a class change, fixing stale level-255 labels.

Skills earned through play

Eligible skills unlock at their usual levels, starting at 1. Improve them through use or training with trainers for your held classes. The extra-class training and offhand correction is deployed; the reported player issue was confirmed resolved.

Extra-class skills and combat hotbuttons

Eligible skills appear in Actions → Abilities and can be assigned to hotbuttons. Extra-class Monk attacks, disciplines and dual wield use your held-class eligibility and native requirements. Owning a class does not grant maximum skill.

10% passive AA while leveling

With ability focus off, eligible kills and quest/task rewards give full normal leveling experience plus 10% of their full ability-experience award. Nothing is taken away from leveling. The live rate changed from 20% to 10% on October 17. Tiny awards can round down; saved progress carries toward the next point. The current conversion is 1,000,000 AA experience per point; ability purchase prices still vary. The threshold increased from 40,000 to 1,000,000 after the October 21 live pacing review. Raw partial experience is retained: 2,000 XP now means 0.2% of the next point rather than 5%. The AA conversion change preserves ordinary leveling XP and existing purchases. Retiring the XP package separately removes its +50% bonus to normal and AA gains.

Allowed AA ranks open at level 1

Every rank in Nightcap’s allowed AA pool is available from level 1. Your held classes, eligibility, prerequisite ranks and earned points still govern purchases; this is not unrestricted access to every EverQuest AA.

Use #aaexp off for normal leveling plus passive ability gains, or #aaexp on to send eligible experience entirely to abilities. Full focus receives no additional passive bonus. Partial allocations become 100%. Use #aaexp to check your setting.

A Class column in the ability window

The ability window identifies class origins in a dedicated Class column across its four tabs, making a multiclass build easier to browse.

Extra-class changes and ability refunds

The Chronicler can remove an extra class, refund eligible earned ability points, and adjust skill limits. Shared abilities and scribed spells remain; your remaining classes govern spell use. Try a spare character first while this is being tested.

A useful starting kit

New characters begin in the tunnel with 100 platinum, a starting-class weapon, and a robe with 10 armor class and +5 to their main stat. These are one-time creation rewards.

Find useful early AAs

Update through launcher Play, then open Alternate Advancement and turn on Recommended AA beside Can Purchase. It starts off and shows up to ten next steps across your held classes, favoring early survival, sustain and useful damage. The reason column explains each choice; missing prerequisites and later skills or pets are labeled. Native filters still apply, so Can Purchase can narrow the list further. Turn Recommended AA off to browse the full legal catalog. Recommendations do not unlock extra AAs, change prices or buy anything automatically.

Reuse belongs to the ability

Different activated AA families keep separate cooldowns across your held classes; ranks of one family share reuse. Reconnecting or changing ranks does not erase a remaining wait. See cooldown repairs and current limits.

All-class AA update

The released catalog contains 1,845 allowed ranks across 489 ability lines, up by 676 ranks. Availability follows your held classes, earned points and prerequisites. Existing purchases, free starter ranks and the recent pet/melee limits remain. Logging in does not grant points or paid ranks.

Druid can buy all six existing ranks of Healing Boon, which improves heal-over-time critical chance. Bard gains Dance of Blades and Hastened Blades; these retain finite native durations and reuse. Wizard gains its Destructive Fury line; when two versions apply, the higher native critical-damage contribution wins.

This is a rank and access update. Some native effects differ from THJ custom abilities, and unverified custom behavior, fixed-damage executes and later free starter ranks remain restricted. Gameplay and encounter balance checks continue.
